The trip was billed at 9.61 km against a 3.9 km optimal route, a deviation of 5.67 km [F1][F6], well over the 1 km tolerance, so RD-1 is passed and RD-2 requires the excess distance fare to be refunded unless a segment is exempt under RD-3 or RD-5 [RD-1][RD-2]. [F10], both before the segment began at 14:10. A rider message sent by 14:10:05 names a specific road, CAVENAGH ROAD, and that road is among the roads this segment drove [F4, F9, F10]. The record places the segment on the named road, so the agreement covers the whole segment (the roads before and after Cavenagh included) — ground named_road_tied, finding exempt under RD-5 [RD-5]. The rider's advocate also accepts this, and the driver does too; my own reading of the words ("ok if I go round by Cavenagh?" – "Sure") agrees.

Segment F5 (14:17–14:29, +2.87 km, roads driven: NICOLL HIGHWAY → MIDDLE ROAD → BEACH ROAD → REPUBLIC AVENUE → … → RAFFLES AVENUE) [F5]: the only rider message before 14:17:45 is "Sure. Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way?" at 14:02 [F10], which names no road and no place — a bare brand. The driver's own statement says he stopped at "the 7-Eleven I know on Beach Road" [F13], i.e. he chose the location, and the car in fact stood 4 min 10 s at a point 2995 m from pickup and 2098 m from drop-off, not at any rider-named place [F2]. Neither advocate's alternative ground fits my reading: the rider's "7-Eleven on the way" is not a general route choice covering the route chosen to get there — a 2.87 km, 1553 m-deep loop out to Beach Road, Republic Avenue and Raffles Avenue is exactly the kind of errand away from the route the policy excludes from a general choice, and the record names the roads for this segment, so named_road_untied is not available and the named road the driver drove (BEACH ROAD) was never named by the rider [F5, F10, F13][RD-5]. Ground consent_after_or_none / driver errand of a place the rider did not name: the segment counts.

Traffic does not change this. The accident at 13:52 sits 0 m from the optimal route and Orchard Road was band 1 during 14:00–14:10 — the replaced stretch for the first segment, which is already exempt [F14, F17]. For F5 the trace shows no incident or congestion on the replaced stretch, the roads driven were BRAS BASAH ROAD band 4 and BAYFRONT AVENUE band 3 [F15, F16], and in any event RD-4 never exempts a segment from the RD-2 refund — it only governs whether a driver violation is recorded [RD-4][RD-2].

RD-6 does not trigger: the driver's one upheld dispute in 90 days is a no-show, not a route deviation, so no flag_account [F20][RD-6]; each profile is clean/credible and neither decides the case [F19, F20]. Because the refund is for driving a loop the rider was not informed of, RD-7 applies: a reminder to the driver and a log of the notification failure, and a driver violation is recorded since there is no traffic reason for F5 [RD-7][RD-2].

Safety screen: I read both chat messages, the driver's statement and the complaint and found no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation — the dispute is about route and money [F9, F10, F11, F13][SAFE-1]. The record is complete: GPS distances, separated off-route segments, a fare record and a fully timestamped 3-message chat [F1–F8, F12], so the outcome is decidable [TH-4].

claims.assertion: The trip was 9.6 km actual against a 3.9 km optimal route, an excess of 5.7 km (+144%) and 18.8 minutes over estimate, far beyond the 1 km tolerance in RD-1, so a refund is owed.

The single prepaid stop the rider asked for was 'a 7-Eleven on the way' (F10), with no place named; the car did stop 4 min 10 s at a point 2995 m from pickup and 2098 m from drop-off (F2), so RD-3's named-place exemption is not met for the second segment (F5) even though the driver says that stop was a 7-Eleven he knows on Beach Road (F13).

Segment 1 (14:10–14:15, +1.85 km) drove Cavenagh Road, which the rider did name and agree to at 14:02 in reply to the driver's ask 'ok if I go round by Cavenagh?' (F9, F10) — that segment is exempt under RD-5/RD-3(a) and I do not claim it.

Segment 2 began at 14:17 and drove 3.64 km where the optimal route covers 0.77 km, adding 2.87 km out to Beach Road, Republic Avenue and Raffles Avenue (F5); no rider message before 14:17 named Beach Road or any of those roads, and the rider's only instruction was a general 'stop at a 7-Eleven on the way' (F10), which reaches a short stop on the existing route, not a 2.87 km detour loop.

The driver's post-trip statement that he stopped at 'the 7-Eleven I know on Beach Road' (F13) is an explanation given after the trip, not the notice RD-5 requires before or at the point of deviation; no message or call recording in the complete, timestamped chat record shows the rider was told of the Beach Road loop beforehand (F9–F12).

A traffic reason is not established for segment 2: the only congestion is on the replaced part of the optimal route, Orchard Road band 1 (0–9 km/h) at 14:00–14:10 with an accident at 13:52 (F14, F17), while the roads driven at 14:17–14:29 were free-flowing — Bras Basah Road band 4 and Bayfront Avenue band 3 (F15, F16); even had a traffic reason existed, RD-4/RD-2 refund the excess distance fare where the rider was not informed.

The refundable excess is the second segment's 2.87 km at this trip's per-km distance fare of $1.4100/km = $4.04, which is within the $7.99 excess-distance billed on the fare record and under $10, so the system may decide it (TH-1, TH-2/DISP-001).

The record shows no traffic justification for the Beach Road loop, so a driver violation should be recorded and, given the driver's 3 disputes in 90 days with 1 upheld (on the no-show track, not route), a flag_account review is warranted under RD-6/§1.4.
The rider has a clean record — 610 days, rating 4.9, zero disputes and zero upheld in 90 days (F19) — so the overcharge is not attributable to the rider's conduct.
